transcript.statement: The proposed requirements ensure ethical handling of attendance data, complying with regulations like GDPR (RES-01) and promoting transparency (RES-02). Allowing students to dispute records (RES-03) ensures fairness, while anonymizing reports (RES-04) protects identities. Timely notifications (RES-05) maintain accountability, and role-based access control (RES-06) safeguards sensitive data. Finally, maintaining historical data (RES-07) is crucial for compliance and analysis. These requirements align with ethical standards and protect student rights.

transcript.statement: The TrustworthinessAgent's requirements emphasize the security and privacy of student attendance data. Encrypting data (TRU-01) ensures protection against unauthorized access, while role-based access control (TRU-02) restricts data access to authorized users. Maintaining an audit log (TRU-03) enhances traceability, and allowing students to view their records post-authentication (TRU-04) promotes transparency. Implementing checksums (TRU-05) ensures data integrity, while mechanisms to report breaches (TRU-06) empower users. Session timeouts (TRU-07) further protect against unauthorized access. These requirements collectively ensure a secure and trustworthy system for handling sensitive attendance data.

transcript.statement: The SafetyAgent's requirements prioritize the secure handling of attendance data, ensuring that unauthorized access is prevented (SAF-01) and that data integrity is maintained through real-time synchronization (SAF-02) and automated alerts for discrepancies (SAF-03). transcript.statement: The GreenAgent's requirements focus on minimizing the environmental impact of the RollCall system. Real-time attendance updates using low-energy protocols (GRN-03) contribute to overall resource savings. transcript.statement: The EfficiencyAgent's requirements ensure optimal performance of the RollCall system. requirements.text: The system shall ensure secure authentication and encryption of user data to prevent unauthorized access.
The system shall implement a unified role-based access control system that ensures data anonymization and security.
The system shall maintain historical attendance data for a minimum of five academic years with optimized storage.
The system shall provide a formal dispute process for attendance records while optimizing data storage.
The system shall ensure real-time processing of attendance data across multiple classes while maintaining data accuracy.
The system shall implement enhanced logging mechanisms for auditing attendance modifications.
The system shall notify users of their carbon footprint based on attendance patterns.
The system shall allow students to view their attendance records only after successful authentication.
The system shall generate attendance reports within 5 seconds for up to 1000 students.
The system shall maintain a logging mechanism for all access and modifications to attendance records.
The system shall provide a user interface that responds to user interactions within 1 second.
The system shall store historical attendance data for a minimum of five academic years to support long-term analysis.
